summary: Token scope header canonicalization at identity-proxy collapses scopes causing API 403 in private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 403s from inference API calls even though the same service account token was used successfully minutes earlier. The failures started after a scheduled upgrade to the customer's edge NGINX-based ingress and coincided with service-account rotation events.

Impact:
- Affects Cyclone Health private deployment in us-west-2.
- Token-based requests to /v1/inference return 403 Forbidden for some requests from the same client during a short window (~30-90s) after token refresh.
- Customer has degraded automation: nightly model scoring jobs fail intermittently.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed ingress + Redwood private control plane)
- identity-proxy v1.14.2 (customer bundle) fronted by NGINX 1.22 as edge ingress
- Service account tokens minted by Cyclone Health IdP via OIDC token-exchange flow

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer runs automated job that exchanges an IdP assertion for a Redwood service token via token-exchange endpoint through identity-proxy.
2) Immediately after rotation, job makes several parallel inference requests using the new token.
3) ~20-40% of requests receive 403. Subsequent retries usually succeed after ~5-30s.

Observed behavior:
- Support trace shows token introspection passes at control plane, but RBAC policy evaluation fails because the token's "scope" claim in the effective JWT is missing the required permission scope (redwood.inference.invoke).
- Raw upstream IdP token contains scope as a single space-delimited string: "scope": "openid profile redwood.inference.invoke"
- After passing through customer's ingress + identity-proxy, the token-exchange layer emits a token where the scope claim appears as a comma-delimited or collapsed single token value (examples below). RBAC engine treats the transformed scope as one atom and denies access.

Expected behavior:
- Scope claim should preserve space-delimited scopes or an array of scopes so RBAC evaluation can correctly match required scope values. No 403s for valid tokens.

Logs / Evidence (sanitized):
- IdP issued JWT (decoded claim): {
  "sub": "svc-12345",
  "scope": "openid profile redwood.inference.invoke",
  "exp": 1700007200
}
- Token post-exchange observed in control-plane header (decoded claim): {
  "sub": "svc-12345",
  "scope": "openid,profile,redwood.inference.invoke",
  "exp": 1700007200
}
- identity-proxy access log excerpt (sanitized):
  - 2026-02-20T16:12:09Z "POST /v1/token-exchange" 200 512 "token_id=***"
  - 2026-02-20T16:12:09Z "POST /v1/inference" 403 142 "svc-12345 scope=openid,profile,redwood.inference.invoke"

Initial hypothesis:
- NGINX or an upstream header normalization step is merging multiple 'scope' header values into a single comma-separated header before token-exchange completes, and the identity-proxy/translator is mapping headers back into JWT claims incorrectly (using header splitting by comma instead of preserving a space-delimited scope string).
- The problem manifests under parallel requests following a token rotate when multiple components re-emit headers simultaneously.

Temporary workarounds tried by customer:
- Reverting ingress to pre-upgrade NGINX resolved the errors temporarily for them.
- Customer configured their IdP to emit scopes in a single long string (works but not acceptable long-term for other tooling).

Next steps / action items:
1) Support reproduced locally using a test harness with NGINX proxy config that collapses repeated headers; reproduced failing RBAC evaluation. (Assigned to Omar Singh)
2) Engineering to propose fix in identity-proxy to canonicalize scope claim consistently (accept both comma- and space-delimited, and prefer preserving original token scope if present). PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/789
3) Recommend a short-term policy change in RBAC engine to accept comma-delimited scope atoms as equivalent to space-delimited ones while fix rolls out. (Linked INT-4412)
4) Coordinate staged rollout and customer patching schedule.

Customer notes:
- They prefer a fix on the identity-proxy that is defensive rather than requiring IdP changes.
- They provided config snippets for their NGINX changes; attached in comments.
comments: 2026-02-20T17:05Z - Maya Chen (Support): Opened ticket after customer provided traces and JWT samples. Noted correlation with their ingress upgrade. Asked SRE to reproduce locally.

2026-02-20T19:12Z - Omar Singh (SRE): Reproduced failure in lab with NGINX config that sets proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization and enables proxy_buffering; observed header merging behavior. Created reproducer and assigned to eng for fix. Linked PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/789.

2026-02-21T09:45Z - Elena Park (Auth Eng): Investigating RBAC evaluator to add tolerance for comma-separated scopes. Initial patch will be a fallback match to reduce customer impact. If accepted, will ship as hotfix to control plane for private customers.

2026-02-21T11:30Z - Cyclone Health (Customer): Thank you for the quick triage. Reverting ingress upgrade restored jobs but we cannot stay on old version long-term. Please provide ETA for patch and mitigation steps we can apply in their NGINX until patch is available.

2026-02-22T08:20Z - Omar Singh (SRE): Rolled a canary hotfix to one internal staging tenant that normalizes 'scope' claim by converting commas to spaces when reconstructing claims from headers; observed no regressions. Preparing release notes and customer-facing mitigation guidance.
resolution: In Progress - hotfix canary applied to staging. Engineering patch in identity-proxy to preserve original scope formatting and RBAC evaluator updated to accept comma-separated fallback. Planned customer hotfix rollout on 2026-02-24 after QA. Customer workaround: revert ingress or configure IdP to emit single scope string.
resolution_notes: Patch reference: identity-proxy v1.14.3-hotfix (PR #789). RBAC tolerant match behind feature flag for private control plane (FLAG: rbac.scope_comma_fallback=true). Post-deploy follow-up: audit logs to ensure no unintended permission expansion; add unit tests for scope parsing edge-cases.
follow_up: 1) Post-release validate Cyclone Health production job runs for 48h. 2) Remove fallback flag after identity-proxy fix is rolled to all private tenants and we validate no other customers rely on comma-separated semantics. 3) Add a runbook entry for scope-header canonicalization issues.
